newsitem.title: UK: British oil, gas tax receipts jump 50 pct.
newsitem.headline: British oil, gas tax receipts jump 50 pct.

text.p: British oil and gas tax receipts jumped over 50 percent last year and gas reserves recovered to levels not seen since the boom years of the 1980s, the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) said on Monday.
Government revenue from the sector rose to 3.6 billion pounds sterling in the fiscal year 1996/97 from 2.35 billion stg the year before, the DTI said in its annual "Brown Book" review.
Natural gas production surged 19 percent to a record 89.9 billion cubic metres in 1996 but exploration and development activity boosted reserves.
"Maximum remaining gas reserves stand at some 1,960 billion cubic metres - a level not seen since 1986," UK energy minister Lord Fraser said.
Oil production was broadly unchanged at 130 million tonnes and possible remaining reserves of oil were estimated to be some 2,025 million tonnes, the DTI said.
Total income in the sector rose to about 21 billion stg last year from 18 billion in 1995.

Oil and gas companies gross trading profits, including service contract firms, soared to 14.4 billion pounds sterling from 11 billion stg in 1995, while investment rose 3.5 percent to 4.4 billion stg, the DTI said.
Oil and gas production in 1998 accounted for some 2.5 per cent of Britain's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) and was estimated to have contributed a positive 4.9 billion stg to the balance of payments.
Development activity reached new record levels with 261 wells drilled in 1996, compared with 244 in 1995. Sixteen new offshore fields were brought onstream, compared to only six in 1995.
A total of 112 exploration and appraisal wells were drilled in 1996, compared with 98 in 1995.
